transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well, uh, I guess what really brought me in is... my wife, mostly. She'll be standing there telling me about my cousin’s appointments, or figuring out who's giving him rides. Which is a whole ordeal, by the way. He’s got this old Buick that’s always breaking down, and I keep telling him, you know, just get a Toyota or a Honda, it'll run forever. I had a Civic back in the nineties that got to two hundred thousand miles without a single issue. Great gas mileage, too, especially back when gas wasn't an arm and a leg. 

But anyway, he won't listen. So she's organizing his rides, and she'll be talking to me about the schedule, and I’m looking right at her... but then a minute later I realize I didn’t actually take in half of what she just said. I'm looking right in her eyes, but the words just don't stick.
Would you say you've had trouble like this focusing and staying on track since you were a kid, or is this something new that's developed recently?

Well, no, it's not new. It's... it's been like this for as long as I can remember. Even way back in grade school, definitely before I was 12. My parents used to go to those parent-teacher conferences, you know? And they'd always come back with the same story. The teachers would say I was bright, but I was just always daydreaming. Looking out the window. 

Actually, I remember my fourth-grade classroom had these huge windows that looked right out onto the playground, and past that was this big oak tree. We used to try to climb it during recess, but old Mr. Henderson—he was the principal, wore these terrible plaid suits—he'd always come out and yell at us to get down. He had this booming voice, you could hear it all the way from the cafeteria. 

But yeah, the teachers would tell my folks I was always leaving my homework in my desk, or I'd need constant reminders just to finish whatever worksheet we were supposed to be doing. So, it's definitely not a new thing, just... maybe catching up with me more now.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed feeling persistently down, anxious, or worried, separate from the difficulty focusing you've described?

No, not really. I mean, I don't feel down or anything like that. Just... scattered, I guess. It's funny you mention worrying, though, because my neighbor, Phil, he's a worrier. Oh boy, is he. The man practically lives at the window, watching the street. Just last week, the city came by to trim the branches near the power lines, and Phil was out there in his bathrobe—at two in the afternoon, mind you—yelling at the guys in the bucket truck. He was convinced they were going to drop a branch on his prize-winning hydrangeas. He's got these massive blue ones, they really are beautiful. He says the trick is coffee grounds in the soil, but I tried that once and it just attracted ants. Anyway, no, I'm not really an anxious guy myself. Just frustrated with my own brain sometimes.
